turns.text: How have your evenings been since we last spoke?
Work keeps following me home. Even after I close the laptop, I’m thinking about what I missed or what someone might ask me tomorrow.
What do you usually do when those thoughts show up?
Check my phone. Sometimes there isn’t even a message. I just look anyway, and then the evening disappears.
Have there been any evenings that felt different?
On Tuesday I put an album on while making dinner. I still thought about work, but I enjoyed parts of the evening. I also spoke to my sister on Sunday, which felt good.
What was meaningful about that conversation?
We weren’t solving anything. We were just catching up. It reminded me that there are things in my life besides work.
What other things would you like to make room for?
Drawing, perhaps. I used to keep a sketchbook. A short walk could be nice too, especially when I’ve spent the whole day indoors.
Would you like to choose one of those now, or leave the choice open?
Leave it open. Calling my sister, drawing, listening to music, and walking all sound possible. What feels right will depend on the day.
How about making space for one enjoyable or meaningful activity before our next session?
I’m up for giving that a go. I’ll make time for one thing this week and choose the activity when I’m ready.
Would setting a particular day help?
I’d rather keep it flexible. Thursday is busy because I pick up my niece. I don’t want to turn all those ideas into separate tasks.
One activity of your choice, with the day left open.
Exactly. That feels doable.
You’ve also said it’s difficult to remember how the week felt when you get here. Would recording your mood help you look back?
Let’s do that. I’ll log my mood each evening around eight, thinking about the day as a whole.
What rating format would you use?
Zero to ten makes sense to me. Zero would be my worst day, and ten my best.
You mentioned low energy earlier. Would you like to record that too?
Yes, include energy. I’d also like to track my sleep quality and motivation alongside mood. I want to see what I notice over the week.
We also practised a breathing exercise together today. What was that experience like for you?
My mind wandered, but I could come back to it. I noticed my shoulders felt less tight afterward.
Would you like to repeat that same exercise between sessions?
That sounds manageable. I’ll practise the breathing exercise we did today for three minutes each day.
Is there a time that would fit?
After I finish work would be a useful point to try it. I don’t need a reminder at a particular clock time.
Would you like to note your tension before and afterward, or simply record how the practice went?
I can add the tension ratings when I feel like it. Some days I might just write a few words about what happened.
Do you have a recording of the exercise?
No, but I remember the one we practised. I’ll use that.
We also mentioned journaling earlier. Is that something you want to start now?
Not this week. I already have enough to work with.
What would you like to revisit next time?
How the evenings felt, whether I made room for something I enjoyed, and what I noticed when I tried the breathing practice. The mood entries should help me remember.
We can start there next time.
